newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures pare gains, still end up.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures pare gains, still end up.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared early gains but still ended higher across the board Monday in moderate trade, driven by talk of firmer cash prices and forecasts for colder Midwest weather later this week.
Spot-December edged up 2.7 cents to close at $2.731 per million British thermal units. January settled 3.2 cents higher at $2.709. Others ended up by 0.3 to two cents.

"It seemed like mostly locals drove us up early, but I think you're going to need some real cold to keep it up," said one Houston-based trader, adding forecasts for colder Midwest weather likely were not enough to drive prices much higher.
Despite forecasts for some below-normal Midwest weather later this week and next, some remained skeptical current levels can be sustained.

"I don't know where we go from here. They're pricing it as if a cold winter was already here," said one East Coast trader, adding the market could be setting up for a big fall if cold weather expectations are not met early in the season.
But with memories still lingering of last winter's price spikes after stocks fell to record low levels, few expected the bears to be aggressive any time soon.
Technically, traders still pegged December support in the $2.66 area and then in the low-$2.50s. Resistance was seen at today's high of $2.81 and then at the $2.865 contract high.

Cash sources said November Gulf Coast prices were up more than a nickel Monday to about $2.70. November Midcon gas jumped more than a dime to the low-$2.50s. November at the New York city gate gained five to 10 cents to the $3.30-3.40 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 2.5 cents to $2.244. NYMEX said 39,872 Hub contracts traded, down sharply from Friday's revised tally of 83,957.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled 6.5 cents higher at $1.205, while deferreds closed up by four to nine cents. NYMEX said 88 Alberta contracts traded compared with 139 on Friday.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.
NYMEX November Permian natgas finished 13 cents higher at $2.57, while deferreds were untraded but up one to six cents. NYMEX said 75 Permian lots changed hands versus 72 on Friday.
NYMEX November Permian natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.
On the KCBT, November expired 15.8 cents higher at $2.628, while most deferreds ended up by one-half to 8.5 cents. The December East/West spread narrowed by 2.8 cents to 18.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
